qs.q: A surgeon performs an elective low anterior resection for rectal cancer. The bowel is opened under controlled conditions with no spillage of contents. According to the CDC wound classification system, what is the appropriate category for this surgical site?
o: Class I: Clean uninfected surgical site
qs.e: Surgeries involving the gastrointestinal tract under controlled conditions without spillage are classified as clean-contaminated. Class I is reserved for non-inflamed, non-penetrating procedures, while Class III involves major spillage or acute inflammation.
qs.s: Surgical Site Infections: Types, Risk Factors, Wound Classification: MCQs

qs.q: An elective low anterior resection for rectal cancer is planned. Which combined pre-operative preparation is specifically recommended for this procedure?
o: Mechanical bowel preparation with oral antibiotics
Therapeutic enemas every two hours starting the morning before surgery
Complete restriction of all oral intake for three days pre-operatively
High-dose intravenous broad-spectrum aminoglycosides for 48 hours
qs.e: Mechanical bowel preparation with oral antibiotics is recommended for elective colorectal surgery to reduce microbial load. Enemas alone are insufficient without oral antibiotic regimens.
qs.s: Surgical Site Infections: Types, Risk Factors, Wound Classification: MCQs

qs.q: A 52-year-old man undergoes an abdominoperineal resection for a low rectal cancer. What is the most likely indication and type of stoma created in this procedure?
o: Permanent end colostomy to evacuate stool after rectal and anal removal
Permanent end ileostomy to evacuate stool after rectal and anal removal
Defunctioning transverse colostomy to evacuate stool after rectal and anal removal
Temporary loop ileostomy to evacuate stool after rectal and anal removal
qs.e: Abdominoperineal resection involves removing the rectum and anus, making a permanent end sigmoid or descending colostomy the commonest indication. A loop ileostomy is instead used to protect a colorectal anastomosis rather than for rectal excision.
qs.s: Intestinal Stomas: Colostomy and Ileostomy, Types, Care and: MCQs

qs.q: A surgical team is planning the closure of a temporary loop ileostomy in a 40-year-old woman whose primary rectal cancer resection healed successfully three months ago. What is the standard timeframe recommended for closing a loop ileostomy?
qs.e: Typically, a loop ileostomy is closed at 8 to 12 weeks once the primary disease is healed and the patient is nutritionally restored. Closing it at 1 to 2 weeks is too early for adequate anastomotic healing.
qs.s: Intestinal Stomas: Colostomy and Ileostomy, Types, Care and: MCQs

qs.q: A 65-year-old man undergoes an anterior resection for rectal cancer. His preoperative serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level is 120 ng/mL. What does this markedly elevated level most strongly suggest?
o: A high likelihood of synchronous polyps
An early Dukes A mucosal lesion
qs.e: Very high CEA levels above 100 ng/mL strongly suggest that distant metastases are present. CEA is useful for baseline staging and follow-up after resection, but levels do not correlate with synchronous polyps or bowel preparation quality.
qs.s: Colorectal Cancer: Presentation, Staging and Surgical Management: MCQs

qs.q: A 71-year-old man with a resected rectal cancer is being evaluated for long-term prognosis. Which of the following pathological findings is considered a poor prognostic factor?
qs.e: Poorly differentiated histology, raised pre-operative CEA, venous invasion, and positive resection margins are all recognized poor prognostic factors. Negative margins and normal CEA are favorable features.
qs.s: Colorectal Cancer: Presentation, Staging and Surgical Management: MCQs

qs.q: A 66-year-old man has a low anterior resection with a low colorectal anastomosis for a rectal cancer. What surgical intervention is typically performed to protect this vulnerable anastomosis from leakage?
qs.e: A temporary defunctioning loop ileostomy or colostomy protects a low anastomosis and is usually closed after 6 to 8 weeks to 3 months. Permanent colostomies are reserved for abdominoperineal resections.
qs.s: Colorectal Cancer: Presentation, Staging and Surgical Management: MCQs

qs.q: Following a low anterior resection for rectal cancer, a male patient complains of new-onset sexual dysfunction and urinary retention. What is the most likely underlying mechanism for these specific complications?
o: Ischemia of the perineal skin flap
qs.e: Sexual dysfunction and urinary retention after rectal surgery are caused by inadvertent nerve damage during dissection of the mesorectum and pelvic autonomic nerves. They are distinct from chemotherapeutic toxicities or staple line strictures.
qs.s: Colorectal Cancer: Presentation, Staging and Surgical Management: MCQs
